on_screen_text.text: Karoline Leavitt says Trump had plans ready to wipe out all Iranians
WHAT WAS YOUR UNDERSTANDING OF WHAT HE MEANT WHEN HE SAID, "THIS CIVILIZATION IS GOING TO BE ELIMINATED"?

I THINK IT WAS A VERY, VERY STRONG THREAT FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES THAT LED THE IRANIAN REGIME TO CAVE TO THEIR KNEES AND ASK FOR A CEASEFIRE AND AGREE TO REOPENING THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ.
SO IT WAS A VERY STRONG THREAT THAT LED TO RESULTS.
AND AS THE SECRETARY OF WAR STATED AT THE PENTAGON THIS MORNING, IT WAS NOT AN EMPTY THREAT BY ANY MEANS.
THE PENTAGON HAD A TARGET LIST THAT THEY WERE READY TO HIT GO ON AT 8:00 PM LAST NIGHT IF THE IRANIAN REGIME HAD NOT AGREED TO OPEN THE STRAIT, WHICH THEY DID.
AND I THINK THAT'S SOMETHING WE SHOULD ALL BE GRATEFUL FOR.
WH: STRAIT OF HORMUZ MUST REMAIN OPEN

spoken_summary: An unnamed reporter asks Karoline Leavitt for her understanding of what Donald Trump meant when he said a "civilization is going to be eliminated." Leavitt characterizes it as a "very, very strong threat" that forced the "Iranian regime to cave to their knees" and agree to a ceasefire. She asserts it was not an "empty threat," claiming the Pentagon had a "target list that they were ready to hit go on" if Iran had not complied.
audio_music: The audio consists solely of dialogue from the news broadcast clip, with no music or sound effects.
editing_pacing: The video is a single, continuous clip from a news broadcast. The editing is minimal, featuring one cut from a split-screen view to a single shot of the speaker. Large, bold yellow text appears on screen, timed to the words being spoken.
central_claim: Karoline Leavitt confirms that the Trump administration had concrete military plans to attack Iran, which she describes as a credible threat that achieved its diplomatic goals.
intended_effect: To shock the viewer and portray the Trump administration as dangerously extreme and willing to contemplate mass killing.
uncertainty_flags: Karoline Leavitt refers to a 'Secretary of War.' The United States has not had an official with this title since 1947; the modern equivalent is the Secretary of Defense. It is unclear if this is a slip of the tongue or a reference to a different role.
